name: sloth-ownership-safe-kubernetes-resource-1680
instr:
Sloth cannot safely converge every Kubernetes object emitted by a transform, including heterogeneous results. Make real, dry-run, and fake controller modes report the same desired-versus-live outcome while preserving their mutation guarantees and offline YAML behavior.

Give every transformed object a stable group, version, resource, namespace, and name identity. Planning must be deterministic and ordered by `ResourceIdentity`. Classify `ReconcileCreate` as `create`, `ReconcileUpdate` as `update`, `ReconcileUnchanged` as `unchanged`, `ReconcileDelete` as `delete`, and `ReconcileConflict` as `conflict`. Foreign objects return `ErrResourceOwnershipConflict` with `resource ownership conflict`, remain untouched, and prevent completion.

`ApiserverRepository` applies the full report. `DryRunApiserverRepository` derives it from current reads without status, create, update, or delete writes. `FakeApiserverRepository` reproduces discovery, conflicts, updates, and pruning locally. Expose these with `PlanReconciliation`, `Inventory`, `DeleteSLOResources`, `NewApiserverRepository`, `NewDryRunApiserverRepository(svc, logger)`, and `NewFakeApiserverRepository` from `github.com/slok/sloth/internal/storage/k8s`.

Retries must replan from live state, avoid completed mutations, and converge without duplicate writes. Record `ReconciliationFinalizer` as `sloth.slok.dev/resource-cleanup` before the first successful managed write. Keep it during deletion until inventory is empty.
